about: What each statement of journal/beginning-to-end.md (the journal's closing piece) rests on: incident.ci@'s data, the accountant's books, the board, the brief, the reporter's traces and the journal's other pieces. Resolved on every build by tools/journal-build.mjs.
status: open until the hand-over to business as usual

claims.text: Each agent owns its folders, each push passes one gate, and a push is served in about half a minute.

supports.contains: each owns its folders
node admin/build/validate.mjs   # the gate

claims.text: Web Summit called off its second day on the government's advice (the incident's headline).

supports.contains: Web Summit calls off Day 2 (Wednesday) on the government's advice

claims.text: Dinis asked by voice for a separate team with its own conductor, repository and site, a newsroom for people and a data source for agents.

supports.contains: A newsroom for people and a data source for agents on Storm Charles

claims.text: The repository's first commit is stamped 21:03:38 UTC; the first push was live at 21:14:33.
He came back six more times before 03:00 UTC.

supports.contains: He then came back six more times before 03:00 UTC

claims.text: By incident.ci@'s read of 10:18 UTC: 920 commits by 31 agents, 830 workflow runs, 596 tagged versions, a median of 37 s from push to served.
What exists is listed in REALITY.md.
Dinis's last direction of the night was at about 02:50; his next words in the record came 6 h 41 min later.

supports.contains: you can use up to $20 in budget

claims.text: At 07:16:30 IPMA lowered Lisbon's wind warning; the row, data, front page, headline and five stories followed within 37 minutes; one wrong 'unchanged' corrected by its author in 51 s.
A source's terms forbade what the site did; the conductor held the reading as an interim measure until Dinis could answer.

supports.contains: The first decision to stop

claims.text: By the accountant's books of 09:41 UTC: 1.06 dollars of model calls through the ledger against a cap of 20 a day.
1.92 billion tokens across the 27 agents measured, 98.6 per cent of them cache reads (agents re-reading their own sessions).
The busiest hour was 02:00 UTC, in money and in tokens.
Agents began handing over to fresh sessions with a short briefing pack.

supports.contains: No person acted between the sentence and the sixth hand-over.

claims.text: At 02:53 the provider's account ran out of credit: the models stopped and nothing else did.

supports.contains: out of credit since 02:53:57 UTC

claims.text: The mistakes of the night, with who found each and what rule it changed, are in Mistakes made in the open.
This journal's own first page carried a wrong count of the cards waiting on Dinis and was corrected by its author within minutes.

supports.contains: **Corrected at 03:03 UTC.**
The board's figure was 36

claims.text: At 10:35 UTC the board counts 44 open cards waiting on Dinis.

supports.why: counted by this agent from board/items/*.json at 10:35 UTC (state not done, closed or answered; waiting_on === 'Dinis'); the board recounts on every build

claims.text: Among them: the provider's account, still out of credit, and the hold on reading Web Summit's site.
When he came back he answered how vault keys are held and asked for page views, a front page for newcomers tried by four invented readers, this story told, flights and transport.

supports.contains: each agent makes its own vaults and sends the conductor a sealed copy of each key
## Dinis, 11 November, ~10:25 UTC: flights and transport
